charts.name: Trinidad and Tobago reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: This pack found no legal chart of accounts in Trinidad and Tobago, and opened neither the Companies Act nor the Corporation Tax Act: no section of either is cited. What the Value Added Tax Act asks of a registered person is a tax invoice (s. 36) and books and records kept at the principal place of business (s. 38 and the Books and Records Regulations). This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of a statement of financial position and an income statement presented in the manner of IFRS for SMEs, which is a choice of this pack and not a text the country imposes. The settlement account of the VAT return (2100, refundable 1172) is distinct from the accounts the tax posts to (2101 collected, 1170 and 1171 recoverable). See README.md

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, s. 36(2)(b) — a tax invoice carries an identifying serial number and the date on which it was given; s. 36(1) — a registered person making a commercial supply above twenty dollars gives the recipient a tax invoice; s. 37 — credit and debit notes. The Act, as read for this pack, does not say that the series may have no gap, which is why `numbering` is `sequential` and not `gapless`; `number_format` is a convention this pack proposes

payment_terms.legal_reference: No text of Trinidad and Tobago read for this pack sets a payment term between two businesses or a rate of interest on a commercial debt paid late: the penalty of eight per cent and the interest of two per cent a month or part of a month (s. 54) are charges on a person who owes the Board, not terms between two businesses. `legal_payment_days` and `late_payment_reference` are empty

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, s. 17(1) — a supply takes place when an invoice for it is given by the supplier, when payment is made for it, or when the goods are made available or the services rendered, whichever is the earlier (the special cases of s. 17(2) to (4), hire purchase, continuous services and progress payments, are not modelled). `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment` is the nearest value of the closed vocabulary: it leaves out the invoice date, which s. 17(1)(a) also makes a tax point, and is to be checked by a reviewer

einvoicing.legal_reference: No text of Trinidad and Tobago read for this pack obliges a business to issue or accept an electronic invoice: the Value Added Tax Act, s. 36, asks for a tax invoice with the particulars it lists, on paper or otherwise, without naming a platform, a format or a Peppol profile. No Peppol authority for the country was looked for. `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null: there is no domestic profile to name

not_taxed.legal_reference: Not modelled, and not a finding that the service is untaxed. Under s. 16(2) and (3) of the Value Added Tax Act a supply by a supplier not resident in Trinidad and Tobago is, as a rule, regarded as not taking place there, and the tax on services is charged only on 'prescribed services' (s. 6(b), s. 14(1)); the reverse charge on services bought from abroad was not found in the text read. Such a purchase is entered with TT-P-EX and the user, with their accountant, checks whether any tax is due outside the pack. See README.md
